prompt:
Extract every policy commitment stated in the text below.

Rules:
- One commitment per line.
- Write each as a verb phrase: an action followed by its object. For example: "raise the income tax threshold" or "build 300000 new homes".
- State each commitment at the level of a distinct policy action, not its implementation details. Do not subdivide a single commitment into steps.
- Include every commitment. Do not select, rank, prioritise, or judge importance.
- Use the text's own terms for policy objects. Do not substitute synonyms.
- Do not number the lines. No bullets, headings, preamble, or commentary.
- If the text states no policy commitments, output the single word NONE.

<text>
Summary of the 2024 manifesto (ideology-free)

Core pledges:
- Freeze non-essential immigration and end small-boat crossings via detention, offshoring, and returns.
- Eliminate NHS waiting lists while keeping services free at point of use.
- Raise the income tax threshold to £20,000; higher rate to start at £70,000.
- Cut energy bills by scrapping green levies and accelerating domestic oil and gas.
- Fund changes by reducing government waste and regulation.

Policy highlights:
- Immigration: Freeze most routes except essential skills; create a new immigration department; process and detain illegal arrivals (offshore if needed); bar asylum from safe countries; deport foreign offenders after sentences; restrict student dependants; require five years’ residence and work before accessing benefits; introduce a higher employer National Insurance rate for foreign workers (exemptions for essential health/care and very small firms).
- Public spending and waste: End interest on commercial bank reserves created by QE; require 5% efficiency savings across departments; cut foreign aid by 50%; expand tax collection capacity; deregulate retained EU rules to spur growth.
- Personal tax and cost of living: Raise the income tax start point to £20,000; cut fuel duty by 20p/litre; scrap VAT on energy and environmental levies; reduce residential stamp duty; restore VAT-free tourist shopping; reform inheritance tax (no IHT below £2m; 20% above).
- Business: Lift corporation tax threshold to £100,000 profit; cut main rate to 20% then 15% (year 3); abolish IR35; raise VAT threshold to £150,000; abolish business rates for high-street SMEs offset by a 4% online delivery tax; simplify and deregulate planning and employment law.
- NHS and social care: Zero basic-rate income tax for frontline NHS and care staff for three years; end training caps; write off clinical student fees pro rata over 10 years’ service; use independent capacity (including abroad) to clear backlogs; introduce tax relief on private healthcare; time-based NHS vouchers; operational efficiency reforms.
- Energy and environment: Scrap Net Zero mandates and renewable subsidies; fast-track North Sea licences and shale test sites; expand small modular nuclear and other technologies.
- Policing and justice: Recruit 40,000 officers; zero-tolerance approach to violent and drug offences; increase criminal justice funding; build 10,000 detention places; review sentencing; reform hate-crime definitions; reopen magistrates’ courts.
- Education: Revise curriculum oversight; ban gender social transitioning in schools and require single-sex facilities; 20% tax relief on independent school fees; scrap interest on student loans and extend repayment to 45 years; tighten entry standards; expand PRUs; require two-year degree options.
- Welfare: Tighten work requirements (two-strike rule on job offers; face-to-face assessments); focus on moving up to 2 million people into work.
- Brexit and governance: Repeal retained EU law; replace Northern Ireland arrangements; reform civil service, House of Lords, postal voting; propose PR referendum; introduce a British Bill of Rights.
- Defence: Raise spending to 2.5% of GDP by year 3 and 3% within six years; pay review; new veterans department; procurement reform; recruit 30,000 for the army; support domestic defence industry.
- Housing: Fast-track brownfield development; prioritise local and contributing residents for social housing; restore mortgage interest relief for landlords; strengthen leaseholder protections.
- Families and children: Introduce a 25% transferable marriage allowance when affordable; front-load child benefit for ages 1–4; mandate single-sex public facilities; address social media harms.
- Transport and utilities: Cancel remaining HS2 (£25bn one-off saving); end ULEZ/LTN schemes; accelerate regional transport; create a 50/50 public–pension fund ownership model for utilities with capped standing charges.
- Agriculture and fisheries: Increase farm budget to £3bn; replace climate-linked farm subsidies with direct payments; curb foreign access to UK waters; rebuild processing; support fleet growth.
- Pensions and care: Establish a social care Royal Commission; tackle offshore tax practices in care; review pensions; reform the Mineworkers’ scheme.

Fiscal plan (estimates):
- Potential annual savings: ~£150bn, plus £10bn from assumed extra growth.
- Annual costs: ~£141bn.
- Headline savings sources include QE interest changes, departmental efficiencies, Net Zero and subsidy cuts, welfare reforms, and reduced aid. Costs arise mainly from tax cuts, health, defence, and policing/justice.
